ai.title: AI settings

views.body: Design is the canvas. Split and Code show the same page as its file. Preview runs the site as a visitor sees it — links and buttons work.

devices.title: Computer, tablet, phone
devices.body: See the page at each width. A setting changed while a tablet or phone is chosen applies only from that width down.

pages.title: Pages and menu
pages.body: Add pages and give them addresses, choose which go in the main menu, and edit the header and footer around every page.

theme.title: The look of the whole site
theme.body: Pick a design kit, then adjust its colours, fonts, corners, spacing and shadows. Every part follows.

mine.title: Your own components
mine.body: A section you build once and reuse on many pages. Change it in one place, and every page that uses it can follow.

agent.title: Ask the assistant
agent.body: Describe what you want — a page, a section, a change — and the assistant builds it here, for you to review.

publish.title: Publish
publish.body: When it looks right, publish: the site is built and goes live. Problems that would break it are listed first.

help.title: Help is here
help.body: This tour again, short tours of single tasks, and the keyboard shortcuts.

section.title: Add a section
section.body: Open Sections and click one — a hero is a good start. It is added to the page.

text.title: Change the words
text.body: Double-click a heading or a text on the page and type. Click outside when you are done.

picture.title: Swap the picture
picture.body: Click a picture on the page. Here, under Content, choose another from your media library.

preview.title: See it as a visitor
preview.body: Press Preview to try the page with working links and buttons.

collection.title: Add a collection
collection.body: In Components, search for Collection and add it. It repeats one design for every item — every event, article or product.

source.title: Choose what it lists
source.body: With the collection selected, choose its content here, and how many items to show.

fields.title: Show the item’s fields
fields.body: Put a heading, text or picture into the collection’s item. In their settings, choose which field of the item each one shows.

detail.title: A page for each item
detail.body: In Pages, give a page an address like /events/:slug and choose its content: it becomes the detail page every item can link to.

mine.title: Your components
mine.body: Components you have made are here, ready to add and to open again.

make.title: Make one from a section
make.body: Right-click a section on the page and choose Make reusable… The component studio opens — the tour goes on there.

settings.title: What pages may change
settings.body: Choose which settings each page gets — a title, a picture, a link — and how they are labelled.

slots.title: Where pages add their own parts
slots.body: Turn an empty area into a slot: each page fills it with its own content.

preview.title: Try it
preview.body: See the component with sample values on a computer, tablet and phone.

versions.title: Versions
versions.body: Pages keep the version they use. Start a new version to change the component without surprising them, then update them when you are ready.

done.title: Back to the page
done.body: Done takes you back to the page, with your component in place.

problems.title: Fix what would break
problems.body: Problems lists what would break the site — a missing page, a picture without a description. Click one to go to it. Errors must be fixed before publishing.

publish.title: Publish
publish.body: Publish saves your work and builds the site. From a draft branch you choose what to take into the release.

deploy.title: Watch it go live
deploy.body: Deployments shows each build, its log and when it is live.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: External APIs your sites can show data from. DCMS calls them with the key, on a schedule, for the operations you list — sites read the stored responses, so the key never reaches a browser.
connections.noneHint: Connect a ticketing, booking or catalogue API to show its data on a visual site.
connections.name: Name
connections.keyStored: Stored — leave empty to keep it
connections.keyHint: Encrypted in Vault and never shown again. Only DCMS’s admin service can use it.
connections.operationsHint: Paths under the base URL, optionally with a query. Only these are fetched; sites read /api/connections/<address name><operation>.
connections.refreshFailed: Some operations failed; their last data is still served.
connections.savedWithErrors: Saved, but some operations failed — see the connection.
connections.confirmDelete: Remove “{{name}}”? Sites using it lose its data.
